props.gloss_en: one does not search [for chametz] by the light of the sun
nor by the light of the moon
nor by the light of a torch
but [one searches] by the light of a lamp
because the light of a lamp is good for the search (the basis term is pesachim_4a_al_mi_livdok's, where Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak gives the same reason for searching at night)
and though there is no proof for the matter, there is an allusion to it, as it is said: 'seven days leaven shall not be found in your houses' (Shemot 12:19)
and it says: 'and he searched, beginning with the eldest' (Bereshit 44:12)
and it says: 'at that time I will search Jerusalem with lamps' (Tzefanyah 1:12)
and it says: 'the lamp of the Lord is the soul of man, searching all the inward chambers' (Mishlei 20:27)
Rava: a courtyard does not require searching
...because the ravens are found there (Steinsaltz: and will certainly eat any chametz there)
Rava: a portico is searched by its own light (Steinsaltz: by the daylight, with no lamp at all)

Rava: what is 'and a brightness is as the light; rays at His side, and there is the hiding of His power' (Chavakuk 3:4)? -- to what are the righteous comparable before the Shekhina? to a lamp before a torch
Rava: a torch for havdala is the mitzva in its choicest form
(entertained) the baraita's sunlight search is that of a courtyard
(entertained) rather, the baraita's sunlight search is that of a portico
no -- [the sunlight clause] is needed for a skylight in a room
(entertained) and where [in the room]? if [the place] opposite the skylight
[the place opposite the skylight] is the portico [case] -- the case of which Rava said אכסדרה לאורה נבדקת
rather, [the sunlight clause speaks] of the sides [of the room]
Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak: this one [the lamp] -- one can put it into holes and cracks; that one [the torch] -- one cannot put it into holes and cracks
Rav Zevid: this one [the lamp] -- its light is before it; that one [the torch] -- its light is behind it
Rav Pappa: with this one [the torch] he is afraid; with that one [the lamp] he is not afraid (Steinsaltz: afraid of starting a fire)
Ravina: this one [the lamp] -- its light is drawn out [steadily]; that one [the torch] -- it is cut off [in flickers]

supports.gloss_en: זכר לדבר, שנאמר: שבעת ימים שאר לא ימצא בבתיכם -- graded by the baraita itself as זכר, not ראיה
ואומר: בעת ההיא אחפש את ירושלים בנרות
ואומר: נר ה׳ נשמת אדם חופש כל חדרי בטן (why this fourth verse is needed is asked at 7b.17-18, the previous unit)

objections.gloss_en: אי נימא בחצר — האמר רבא: חצר אינה צריכה בדיקה, מפני שהעורבין מצויין שם: a courtyard needs no search at all, so the baraita cannot be ruling on how to search one (the memra's reason is p_rava_orvin). Unanswered
אלא באכסדרה — האמר רבא: אכסדרה לאורה נבדקת: a portico IS searched by its own light, so the baraita's ban on sunlight cannot be about it. Unanswered; לא צריכא לארובה דבחדר follows
אי לבהדי ארובה — היינו אכסדרה: the place opposite the skylight is the portico case, which Rava says is searched by its light. Unanswered; אלא לצדדין follows

ואבוקה לא? והאמר רבא: ... למה צדיקים דומין בפני שכינה — כנר בפני האבוקה; ואמר רבא: אבוקה להבדלה מצוה מן המובחר (= p_rava_avuka_havdala, the second ground; the format admits one source per objection). Both memrot rank a torch's light above a lamp's, so why should the baraita exclude the torch? Answered four times, by four voices

answered_by.gloss_en: זה יכול להכניסו לחורין ולסדקין, וזה אינו יכול (= p_rnby_chorin): the lamp can be put into holes and cracks, the torch cannot
זה אורו לפניו, וזה אורו לאחריו (= p_zevid_oro): the lamp's light is before it, the torch's behind it
האי בעית, והאי לא בעית (= p_pappa_beit): with the torch he is afraid, with the lamp he is not
האי משיך נהורא, והאי מיקטף איקטופי (= p_ravina_meshich): the lamp's light is drawn out steadily, the torch's is cut off in flickers
